findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

An employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted with the PIC. Ensure that hand washing is taking place at all times that it is required in the facility.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee was observed to wash their hand and use their bare hand to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to review hand washing with staff to ensure that it is taking place correctly at all times.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

1) A container of milk is observed in the walk in cooler without a date marking and mostly empty. The PC was shown and discarded the container to correct as they were unsure when it had been opened. 2) A containers of pasta sauce is observed with a date of 3/11. This would have the discard date located at the end of 3/18. The PIC was shown and discarded the container to correct. Ensure that all TCS foods are properly date marked and discarded/used prior to the end of day seven.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There were sanitizer buckets observed to be in the kitchen handwashing sink and in the bar handwashing sink. CORRECTED- The PIC moved both of them out of the sink into their respective places. Ensure that handwashing sinks are not used for anything other than the intended purpose of handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There was a container of cooked penne dated 8/14 and a container of coleslaw dated 8/16. CORRECTED- Both food items were discarded due to being past the 7 day date-marking rule. The PICs were educated that any item that is prepared or cooked needs to be date-marked and discarded after seven days (day 1 being the date of opening or preparation).
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).
